=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:72-80 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `phase7_wait_deadline` the deadline is clamped to `job_cap` and then raised back to `floor` (start + budget), so the wait can run past the job-time cap into the finalization reserve.
  WHY: The job's hard timeout can then cut off finalization and cleanup. Severity disagreement: three reviewers rated it MAJOR (mapped to high) and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, calling it a documented, test-pinned trade-off that improves on the pre-PR behavior. The highest severity is used. Gemini cited lines 94-96.
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:156-157 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The comment on the queued-run poll says the queue cap allows up to 30m of waiting, but the default `PHASE7_QUEUE_WAIT_CAP_MINUTES` is 60.
  WHY: It is a comment-only inaccuracy that misleads operators. Two other reviewers (anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash) checked the working tree, found line 157 already says "60m", and judged the finding stale.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:94-96 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The logic in `phase7_wait_deadline` allows the floor (based on the budget) to override the job-time cap.
  WHY: If `floor` exceeds `job_cap`, the wait extends into the finalization reserve, and a hard job timeout can terminate the final steps prematurely.
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:156 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment says the queue cap allows up to 30m of waiting, but the actual default is 60m and it is configurable.
  WHY: It is a documentation-only issue, but it misleads operators troubleshooting runner starvation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:72-80 (phase7_wait_deadline, lines 56-81) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function's comments promise both that every deadline stops E2E_FINALIZATION_RESERVE_MINUTES before the job timeout and that it is never earlier than the old start + budget. The code resolves the conflict in favour of the floor, and `test_job_cap_never_shortens_the_old_budget` (tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_phase7_queue_wait.py:201-208) codifies that.
  WHY: Phase 7 can wait past the finalization reserve and be cut off, with cleanup, by the job's hard timeout when it starts late. This is the same shape as the original release-gate failure (#9794).
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh (comment on the queued-poll sleep branch, "# Poll a queued run every 15 s: the queue cap allows up to 30m of") | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment hard-codes "30m", but the default `PHASE7_QUEUE_WAIT_CAP_MINUTES` was raised to 60 (commit 74daa82).
  WHY: There is no runtime defect, but the comment misstates the worst-case queued wait and goes stale again if the cap is changed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:72-80; tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_phase7_queue_wait.py:212-217 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The deadline is clamped to `job_cap` and then raised to `floor`, so `floor` can override the job-time cap.
  WHY: When Phase 7 starts with less than `PHASE7_WAIT_BUDGET_MINUTES` before the job cap, the wait runs past the finalization reserve, and the job timeout can cut off later finalization or cleanup.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_verify_cancel_on_close.sh:72-80 (clamp at 74-76, floor re-raise at 78-80; open-PR loop initial DEADLINE at line 419) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When a Phase 7 wait starts late, the floor assignment at lines 78-80 raises `PHASE7_WAIT_DEADLINE` back above the job-time cap, so the deadline can overrun the finalization reserve. The open-PR loop's initial DEADLINE behaves the same way on its first iteration.
  WHY: Phase 7 waits into the reserve and the job's hard timeout can kill finalization and cleanup. The reviewer calls this a deliberate, documented trade-off pinned by tests and an improvement on the pre-PR code, which had no job cap.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
